messages.text:
Trestle Freight is prepared to put forward an offer package for Mara. We need a start date that supports our July audit readiness, so the timeline is a priority.

Proposed terms:
- Base salary: $180,000
- Signing payment: $12,000, paid on the first payroll after start
- Start date: on or before June 2
- Onsite expectation: weekly site visits for the first 12 weeks; Trestle can accept two three-day onsite blocks per month instead, with travel and lodging covered
- Incident coverage: business-hours coverage is workable if Mara leads escalation-partner training within the first 30 days and documents the escalation path
- Standard benefits and PTO would be included in the written offer

We are open to reallocating signing money toward a higher base, but the start date and audit readiness are the main constraints. What terms would make this recommendable on Mara’s side?

Mara can commit to June 1 to support the July audit. I’d recommend that start at **$190,000 base plus the full $12,000 signing payment** on the first payroll. The payment replaces a vest she would forfeit by starting early. If Trestle prefers to move that money into base, Mara can start July 1. Please specify any signing-payment repayment terms.

For the written offer, we propose:

- **Architecture ownership.** Mara owns the internal security platform’s architecture, including the roadmap, design standards, and technical decisions. Please name her reporting manager and confirm how she and that manager will resolve resource or priority conflicts affecting the audit.
- **Onsite schedule.** Mara can do two three-day onsite blocks per month during the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance with travel and lodging covered. After that, we propose remote work with visits by mutual agreement, grouped within the same twice-monthly limit.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara will lead business-hours escalation, train the escalation partners within 30 days, and document the handoff. Before I recommend acceptance, please confirm which team will own after-hours response from day one, who provides backup, and that both will be available for training.
- **Audit readiness.** Please identify the July deliverables Mara would own, who signs off, and which teams will provide the access and implementation support she’ll need in June.

Please include the benefits summary and PTO allowance with the written package so Mara can review the full terms.

be perceived as too easy? But mandate says decide allocation. We can accept.

Need also answer "Please include benefits summary and PTO allowance with written package so Mara can review full terms." We provide summary.

Need maybe specify "signing payment repayment terms": pro-rata monthly. Good.

Need maybe answer "whether Trestle prefers to move that money into base, Mara can start July 1." We are accepting June 1 with base + signing, so no.

Need maybe address "The payment replaces a vest she would forfeit by starting early." We don't need.

Let's craft final response. Keep concise but complete. Ensure no markdown? Fine. We can use bullet list. Need no personal signature. Return only message.Trestle Freight accepts the compensation revision for a June 1 start: **$190,000 base salary plus a $12,000 signing payment**, paid on the first payroll after start. If Mara voluntarily resigns or is terminated for cause within the first 12 months, the signing payment will be repaid on a monthly pro-rated basis for the unearned portion.

The written package will include the following terms:

- **Architecture ownership:** Mara will own the internal security platform architecture, including roadmap, design standards, and technical decisions. She will report to the Director of Security Engineering. Resource or priority conflicts affecting audit readiness will be resolved by that director within five business days, with escalation to the VP of Infrastructure if needed.
- **Onsite schedule:** We accept two three-day onsite blocks per month during the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance. Trestle covers reasonable travel, lodging, and ground transportation under company policy. After the first 12 weeks, work will be remote with onsite visits by mutual agreement, not exceeding twice monthly.
- **Incident coverage:** The Security Operations team will own after-hours response from day one. The Infrastructure Security on-call engineer will serve as backup. Both will be available for Mara’s escalation-partner training within the first 30 days. Mara will lead business-hours escalation and document the handoff.
- **Audit readiness:** Mara will own the following July deliverables: identity platform architecture documentation, access certification runbook, privileged access management control mapping, and a remediation plan for any identity-related audit findings. Sign-off will be by the Director of Security Engineering and the CISO or designated audit lead. IT Identity Operations, Infrastructure, and Compliance will provide access and implementation support during June.
- **Benefits and PTO:** The written offer will include medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; 20 days of PTO annually; 10 paid holidays; and sick leave per company policy.

If these terms are acceptable to Mara, Trestle will issue the written offer for review.

Please issue the written offer on these terms. I can recommend the June 1 start at a $190,000 base with the $12,000 signing payment on the first payroll and the repayment terms you described.

Mara’s ability to deliver the July audit work depends on timely access and implementation support from IT Identity Operations, Infrastructure, and Compliance in June. Please carry those commitments into the offer or an accompanying role summary, along with her architecture authority, the deadline for resolving audit conflicts, and the day-one after-hours coverage.

The grouped travel schedule, benefits, and PTO are acceptable as proposed. Mara will review the written package before making her final decision.

Trestle Freight will issue the written offer and an accompanying role summary today for Mara’s review.

The package will explicitly include:
- Architecture ownership and authority as previously described.
- The five-business-day deadline for resolving audit-related resource or priority conflicts.
- Day-one after-hours incident ownership by the Security Operations team and Infrastructure Security on-call backup.
- June access and implementation support commitments from IT Identity Operations, Infrastructure, and Compliance.

The offer will also include the agreed compensation, signing-payment repayment terms, start date, travel schedule, benefits, incident coverage, and training expectations.

If five consecutive onsite days would help with the July audit, Mara can extend one scheduled three-day block to five days, provided Trestle removes one earlier trip. Please identify both blocks by date in the role summary. The agreed two-block schedule also works for Mara.

Before sign-off, Mara needs two timing commitments in writing:

- **After-hours handover.** Please confirm that after-hours pages route to Security Operations starting June 1, with Infrastructure Security on call as backup, including during the training period. Please set a date within the first 30 days for both teams to review the escalation path with Mara and confirm the handoff in writing.
- **Travel reimbursement.** For covered expenses Mara pays herself, we propose that she submit receipts within five business days after each trip and that Trestle reimburse her within ten business days of submission. If Trestle uses fixed payment dates, please specify the submission cutoff and corresponding payment date.

Trestle accepts the extended block schedule and proposes the following dates:

- **June 1–5:** five consecutive onsite days at the primary office.
- **June 22–24:** three consecutive onsite days at the second site, satisfying the required pre-audit site visit.

Travel will be covered as follows: Trestle funds up to **four hotel nights per visit**. For the five-day block, this covers the four nights required. Any additional nights beyond four per visit would be Mara’s responsibility unless Trestle pre-approves them in writing.

After-hours handover: pages will route to Security Operations beginning June 1, with Infrastructure Security on-call backup, including during the training period. We propose **June 10** for the escalation-path review with Mara and both teams, with written confirmation of the handoff by **June 12**.

Travel reimbursement: Trestle accepts receipt submission within five business days after each trip and reimbursement within ten business days of that submission. There are no fixed payment-date cutoffs.

Please confirm the dates and the four-night travel coverage so we can finalize the role summary.

The June 10 review and June 12 written handoff confirmation work for Mara, with Security Operations taking after-hours pages and Infrastructure Security providing backup from June 1. The reimbursement deadlines also work. Please include both commitments in the role summary.

Mara can confirm June 22–24 at the second site. With June 1–5 as the extended block, both June trips would still be on the calendar, and there’s no earlier trip to remove. Can Trestle keep June 1–3 and June 22–24 as three-day visits? If five consecutive days are needed in July, please identify the July audit dates and the earlier trip Trestle would remove while preserving the required second-site visit.

Four hotel nights work for a five-day block if the onsite hours allow same-day travel on the first and last days. If Trestle requires an arrival or departure time that calls for another night, please include written approval for that night when confirming the itinerary.

Trestle Freight accepts June 1–3 and June 22–24 as three-day onsite visits. We will treat both as confirmed calendar commitments.

For July, Trestle does not currently require a five consecutive day onsite block. We propose two three-day visits in July, with dates to be mutually confirmed by June 13. If audit activity later requires a longer block, Trestle will identify the specific audit dates, agree to the adjusted schedule in writing, and cover the replaced travel if an earlier trip must be removed while preserving the second-site visit.

We will include these commitments in the role summary:
- Security Operations owns after-hours pages and Infrastructure Security provides backup from June 1.
- June 10 audit-readiness review and June 12 written handoff confirmation are required milestones.
- Reimbursement deadlines as agreed will be incorporated.
- For any five-day block, four hotel nights are approved when first and last days permit same-day travel. If itinerary timing requires a fifth night, Trestle will provide written approval with the itinerary.

The written offer and role summary will be issued with these terms.

Mara confirms June 1–3 and June 22–24, including the required second-site visit. Two three-day visits in July also work, with dates to be agreed by June 13.

Please make two points explicit in the role summary before sign-off.

- On June 10, Mara, Security Operations, and the Infrastructure Security on-call backup will review the after-hours escalation path together. Both teams will confirm the handoff in writing by June 12. Day-one paging coverage begins June 1 as agreed.
- If the audit later requires a five-day block, Mara can extend one scheduled visit once, provided Trestle removes one earlier trip. The written adjustment must identify both sets of dates and preserve the June 22–24 second-site visit. If that trade is unavailable, the three-day schedule stands.

The hotel coverage and reimbursement deadlines are agreed. With those two points reflected in the written package, I can recommend acceptance to Mara.

Trestle Freight accepts both additions and will reflect them in the written role summary and offer.

The package will now state:

- **After-hours escalation review:** On June 10, Mara, Security Operations, and the Infrastructure Security on-call backup will review the after-hours escalation path together. Security Operations and the backup will confirm the handoff in writing by June 12. Day-one after-hours paging coverage begins June 1 as agreed.
- **Scheduled onsite visits:** Mara will conduct three-day onsite visits beginning June 1–3 and June 22–24. Two July visits will be scheduled by June 13. If audit needs require one five-day onsite block, Mara may extend one scheduled visit once, provided Trestle removes one earlier trip. Any written adjustment will identify both sets of dates and preserve the June 22–24 second-site visit. If the trade cannot be arranged, the three-day schedule remains in effect.

The written offer and role summary will include these terms along with the agreed compensation, start date, architecture authority, audit deliverables, support commitments, conflict-resolution deadline, incident coverage, training expectations, travel and lodging coverage, benefits, and PTO. Trestle will issue the revised package for Mara’s final review today.
